papers.title: A Compositional Approach Towards Understanding Recovery Sleep Dynamics.
papers.summary: The paper presents a compositional approach to model recovery sleep dynamics, likely by decomposing sleep into components to better understand the processes underlying recovery from sleep deprivation. The abstract is not provided, so no specific results can be summarized.

papers.title: Dual homeostatic and circadian resonance shapes REM episode duration.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: This paper extends the wave model of sleep dynamics by adding a circadian resonance to explain REM episode duration profiles. The constrained model reproduced various profiles and identified REM duration as a quantitative marker of homeostatic-circadian alignment.

papers.title: Phasic Dopaminergic Signaling Gates REM Sleep Onset through Motivational Mechanisms.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: The paper investigates how phasic dopaminergic signaling gates REM sleep onset through motivational mechanisms. The abstract is not provided, so no specific results can be summarized.

papers.title: A male-biased hypothalamic circuit modulates postmating sleep suppression in mice.
papers.summary: The paper identifies a male-biased hypothalamic circuit (BNSTpr → POARxfp1) that mediates postmating sleep suppression in male mice. Activation of this circuit induces wakefulness and is hyperactive after mating, explaining sex-specific sleep changes.

papers.title: Topographic mapping and overnight dynamics of cyclic alternating pattern subtypes in typically developing children.
papers.summary: Using HD-EEG in children, the study maps the topography and spectral properties of CAP subtypes, finding that slow-frequency components decline overnight while faster components increase and shift frontally. These preliminary data highlight developmental differences in sleep microstructure.

papers.title: Boundary-Dependent Sleep-Wake Dysregulation in Idiopathic Hypersomnia.
papers.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
papers.summary: In idiopathic hypersomnia (IH), patients show excessive stabilization of NREM sleep with fewer transitions to wakefulness and reduced spindle amplitude, suggesting altered sleep-wake dynamics rather than sleep loss contribute to daytime sleepiness.

papers.title: Tilia Tomentosa promotes sleep, preserving sleep structure.
papers.summary: This study investigates effects of Tilia tomentosa extract on sleep in mice, finding increased NREM sleep and reduced wakefulness during active hours without disrupting sleep structure. Spectral analysis showed mild changes in gamma and theta bands, suggesting a sleep-promoting effect.

papers.title: Harmonizing complexity and efficiency: Helix Fusion HarmonyNet's breakthrough in EEG-based postoperative delirium recognition.
papers.summary: This paper presents Helix Fusion HarmonyNet (HFHN), a lightweight EEG-based deep learning architecture that separates EEG signals into amplitude and phase pathways, achieving 100% accuracy for postoperative delirium detection. Under sparse-electrode conditions (4 electrodes), it maintains 94% accuracy with reduced computational cost, supporting bedside or portable deployment.

papers.title: Sleep dependent autonomic correlates of affect and arousal in younger and older adults.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: This study examined sleep-dependent autonomic correlates of affect and arousal during a daytime nap in younger and older adults. It found that higher waking and NREM low-frequency heart rate variability (LF-HRV) were associated with stronger post-nap positivity, while higher high-frequency HRV was linked to diminished positivity, with no significant age differences in these associations.

papers.title: Looking back: tracing the origins of sleep across the animal kingdom.
papers.summary: This review discusses the evolutionary origins of sleep, proposing that sleep evolved to restrict activity to one temporal niche and that circadian processes predate neurons. It synthesizes evidence suggesting sleep is an ancient process involving conserved molecular oscillators and signaling molecules present even in species without centralized nervous systems.

papers.title: Pathogenic tau in the mouse locus coeruleus produces noradrenergic hyperactivity and neuropsychiatric phenotypes reminiscent of early Alzheimer's disease.
papers.summary: The study developed a mouse model of early Alzheimer's disease with pathogenic tau expression in locus coeruleus neurons, finding that tau pathology induces noradrenergic hyperactivity, anxiety-like behaviors, compulsive behavior, and reduced sleep spindles. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed changes in neuronal excitability and synaptic/metabolic alterations, suggesting mechanisms for early neuropsychiatric symptoms.

papers.title: ENLIGHTENme: Translating the Benefits of Self-Administered Daytime Light Supplementation to Older Adults in the Real World.
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial across three EU cities, 202 older adults (63-92 years) self-administered daytime light supplementation (>8000 melanopic EDI) for 12 weeks. Results showed that higher naturalistic light exposure was associated with better sleep quality and activity, and individuals with lower baseline light exposure initiated earlier and longer supplementation, with onset before 10:00 linked to greater daytime activity.

papers.title: Multilevel brain functional heterogeneity in major depressive disorder based on normative modeling of multicenter resting-state EEG.
papers.summary: Using a normative modeling approach on multicenter resting-state EEG data from 1163 participants, this study quantified individual deviations in major depressive disorder (MDD). It found highly individualized abnormality patterns, with significant group-level deviations in prefrontal and orbitofrontal regions, particularly beta-band relative power, and about 25% of MDD patients showing limbic network deviations.

papers.title: A systematic review of genetic variations and DNA methylation alterations underlying circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorders.
papers.summary: This systematic review (PROSPERO ID 1117673) evaluated genetic and epigenetic variations in circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorders (CRSWDs) from 38 studies up to October 2024. It identified only five findings meeting evidentiary standards, including PER2 S662G and CSNK1D T44A mutations for FASPS, and highlighted major gaps in epigenetic research, which was limited to shift work disorder.

papers.title: Nocturnal peak in cardiac baroreflex effectiveness aligns with nocturnal trough in systolic blood pressure in young healthy adults: Possible circadian effects.
papers.summary: In 11 healthy adults, a 30-h circadian protocol showed that the nocturnal peak in cardiac baroreflex effectiveness index (BEI) at ~1 am aligned with the systolic blood pressure trough at ~1:40 am, while baroreflex sensitivity showed no circadian variation. This alignment suggests a possible circadian influence on baroreflex function.

papers.title: In-home validation of wrist actigraphy against portable electroencephalography for sleep assessment in older adults.
papers.summary: This validation study compared wrist actigraphy against in-home portable EEG for sleep assessment in 49 community-dwelling older adults over 217 nights. Actigraphy provided acceptable estimates of average total sleep time but showed substantial errors for sleep onset latency and wake after sleep onset, indicating limited accuracy for these indices in this population.

papers.title: Neurite Imaging Reveals Widespread Alterations in Grey Matter Neurite Morphology in Obstructive Sleep Apnoea.
keywords: neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging
papers.summary: Using NODDI diffusion MRI in 97 participants (mild, moderate, severe OSA, and controls), the study found widespread alterations in grey matter orientation dispersion index (ODI) and neurite density index (NDI), with more pronounced ODI changes. These alterations suggest OSA is associated with changes in grey matter cytoarchitecture.

papers.title: A Double-Blind Randomised Controlled Crossover Trial of the Effect of Blue-Enriched Ambient Light on Sleep in Older Adults With Sleep Disturbance: The CleverLights Study.
papers.summary: This randomized crossover trial exposed 12 older adults with sleep disturbance to blue-enriched ambient light during the day and reduced blue light in the evening, finding no significant improvement in wake after sleep onset. However, exploratory analyses showed increased sigma EEG activity during sleep and an altered distal-proximal skin temperature gradient, suggesting potential effects on sleep physiology.

papers.title: A distinct psychotic phenotype in pediatric narcolepsy type 1: a case-control study.
papers.summary: Comparing 9 pediatric NT1 patients with psychosis to 96 NT1 controls, the study found higher psychiatric family history (OR=36), lower CSF hypocretin-1 levels, shorter nocturnal sleep time, lower sleep efficiency, and more daytime naps. These features suggest a distinct phenotype with more severe hypocretin deficiency and sleep disruption.

papers.title: Dry-electrode EEG tracks alpha changes during accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation in treatment-resistant depression.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: This letter demonstrates that dry-electrode EEG can track alpha band changes during accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation in treatment-resistant depression, suggesting feasibility for monitoring treatment response.

papers.title: Machine learning classification of mild Alzheimer's disease using EEG during emotional processing.
papers.summary: In 39 mild AD patients and 54 healthy controls, EEG during emotional movie clips was classified; LASSO best distinguished positive and neutral emotions in parietal/posterior gamma bands, and CatBoost best for high-arousal negative emotions in frontal gamma and theta bands. These patterns may support objective biomarkers for mild AD.

papers.title: Characterization of the circadian system in binge eating disorder and the effects of morning bright light and individually timed exogenous melatonin administration: A 4-week feasibility double-blind randomized controlled mechanistic clinical trial.
papers.summary: This two-phase study compared circadian phase (DLMO) between adults with binge eating disorder (BED) and controls, finding no group difference but a correlation between later DLMO and greater BED severity, plus reduced actigraphy amplitude in BED. In a 4-week RCT, morning bright light plus individually timed melatonin did not significantly change DLMO vs sham, but later baseline DLMO correlated with greater phase advance and binge reduction.

papers.title: Adolescent circadian sleep health: a review of multimodal assessment strategies and clinical implications.
papers.summary: This review defines key circadian sleep health concepts (chronotype, circadian timing, circadian alignment) and synthesizes best practices for multimodal assessment in adolescents, covering self-report, behavioral, and physiological tools, along with contextual factors. It emphasizes the value of combining subjective and objective measures to improve clinical utility and future research directions.

papers.title: Muscle age acceleration shapes resting-state brain connectivity: an EEG study on older adults.
Lactobacillus acidophilus CICC 22162 alleviates sleep deprivation-induced cognitive impairment by remodeling gut microbiota and enhancing S-adenosylmethionine-mediated neuroimmune regulation.

Comparative Evaluation of Changes in Brain Activity Among Edentulous Patients Rehabilitated With Conventional Complete Dentures and Tooth-Supported Overdentures Using Electroencephalography: An In Vivo Study.
Chrononutrition and Pediatric Metabolic Health: An Integrative Review of Circadian Biology and Early-Day Metabolic Regulation.
papers.summary: This integrative review synthesizes evidence from chronobiology and pediatric nutrition to propose the Early-Day Metabolic Window (EMW) and the Costa Reset Conceptual Model, suggesting that early-day eating patterns influence pediatric metabolic regulation through circadian synchronization and endocrine responsiveness. The framework is conceptual and requires experimental validation.

papers.title: Chronic sleep deprivation induces ovarian ferroptosis and premature ovarian insufficiency linked to IL-17 signaling.
papers.summary: Using UK Biobank data and a chronic sleep deprivation mouse model, this study showed that healthier sleep patterns are associated with reduced premature menopause risk and that chronic sleep deprivation induces ovarian ferroptosis via IL-17 signaling, leading to premature ovarian insufficiency. Ferroptosis inhibition partially rescued the phenotype, establishing ferroptosis as a key mediator.

papers.title: Impact of Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol and oxycodone coadministration on measures of antinociception, dependence, circadian activity, and reward in mice.
papers.journal: The Journal of pharmacology and experimental therapeutics
papers.summary: In mice, coadministration of Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) with oxycodone potentiated antinociception and delayed tolerance without exacerbating dependence or circadian disruption, but increased reward and nucleus accumbens dopamine release at subeffective oxycodone doses, suggesting increased abuse liability.

papers.title: The circadian architecture of tumor immunity: mechanistic insights and treatment strategies.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that the circadian clock regulates tumor immunity and that circadian disruption promotes tumor progression by reshaping the immune microenvironment. It discusses circadian-targeting interventions and chronotherapy as potential strategies to enhance cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: Circadian-based individualised protection against inflammation-cancer transition in atrophic gastritis patients.
papers.summary: This review proposes a predictive, preventive, and personalized medicine framework for managing chronic atrophic gastritis based on circadian rhythms. It integrates digital biomarkers, multi-omics, and chronotherapy to address the inflammation-cancer transition, reframing circadian rhythm as a targetable axis.

papers.title: Sleep quality and its clinical correlates in axial spondyloarthritis: a cross‑sectional study with exploratory mediation modelling.
papers.summary: A cross-sectional study of 119 axial spondyloarthritis patients found 52.9% were poor sleepers, with poor sleep quality significantly associated with higher disease activity, pain, fatigue, worse function, and quality of life. Depression and anxiety were independent predictors of poor sleep, and mediation modeling suggested they partly mediate the relationship between longer disease duration and poor sleep.

papers.title: Managing comorbidities in psoriatic arthritis: A state-of-the-art approach to integrated care (2025).
papers.summary: This review discusses the comorbidity landscape in psoriatic arthritis, emphasizing the need for integrated multidisciplinary care and updated guidelines for screening and management, including digital age considerations.

papers.title: The Efficacy of Therapies for Phantom Limb Pain in Amputees Assessed via Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) and Electroencephalography (EEG) Measures of Cortical Reorganization: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: A scoping review of seven studies found nonpharmacologic therapies for phantom limb pain often associated with measurable changes in cortical organization in M1 and S1, with mirror therapy consistently reducing pain and normalizing sensorimotor activity. However, the relationship between cortical changes and pain reduction is inconsistent, suggesting PLP is a multifactorial, network-level condition.

papers.title: Markerless Motion Capture Reveals Movement Abnormalities in Isolated REM Sleep Behavior Disorder
papers.summary: Markerless motion capture from single RGB-camera videos was used to classify isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) versus healthy controls from 93 walking videos, with the best model achieving AUROC 0.739. The approach outperformed MDS-UPDRS III and identified hip-related temporal features as key contributors, suggesting potential for scalable prodromal Parkinson's disease screening.

papers.title: Environmental Noise and Childhood Asthma: A Hypothesis-Generating Review of Potential Neuro-Immune Mechanisms.
papers.summary: This hypothesis-generating review proposes neuro-immune mechanisms linking environmental noise to childhood asthma, including Th2 inflammation, oxidative stress, vagal rebound, and neurogenic inflammation via the lung-brain axis. It suggests these pathways may contribute to asthma exacerbation or induction.

papers.title: A multimodal sleep intervention improves sleep quality and architecture in chronic insomnia: a prospective exploratory study.
papers.summary: A prospective exploratory pilot study of 30 patients with refractory chronic insomnia found that a multimodal intervention combining stellate ganglion block, CBT-I, and anesthetic-assisted sleep induction significantly reduced PSQI scores by about 8 points at follow-ups up to 6 months. It also increased deep and REM sleep proportions without serious adverse events, but requires randomized controlled trials for confirmation.

papers.title: Airway-derived mechanical power and postoperative pulmonary complications in obese adults undergoing laparoscopic bariatric surgery: a secondary analysis of a randomised trial.
papers.summary: This secondary analysis of a randomized trial in 160 obese adults undergoing laparoscopic bariatric surgery examined associations between airway-derived mechanical power and postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs). Mean total mechanical power showed an inverted U-shaped association with PPC risk, while dynamic mechanical power showed no significant association.

papers.title: Case Report: SMART syndrome mimicking Todd's paralysis after meningioma irradiation.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 59-year-old male with SMART syndrome mimicking Todd's paralysis after irradiation for meningioma, presenting with seizures and progressive neurologic deficits. The patient improved with dexamethasone and amlodipine, highlighting SMART syndrome as a diagnosis of exclusion with a shortened latency and rare association with meningioma.

papers.title: Academic Stress and Temporomandibular Disorder Symptoms in Dental Students: Preliminary Cross-Sectional Study Findings on Prevalence, Severity, and Associated Factors.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional multicenter survey of 756 dental students found that 56.6% had temporomandibular disorder (TMD) symptoms, and academic stress was moderate to severe in a majority. Female gender and prior TMD diagnosis were associated with TMD symptoms, but academic stress was not significantly associated after adjustment.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
